newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas mostly higher as cold drains supply.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas mostly higher as cold drains supply.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were mostly higher Thursday, as cold weather moved into the Northeast and another cold front was expected to arrive in the Midwest early next week, sources said.
Louisiana Gulf prices gained about 20 cents to the low-$4.60s, with deals reported done anywhere from the $4.70s early to the $4.40s late.

Temperatures in the southern plains were still about 15-25 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal but were expected to moderate this weekend. However, another blast of cold air is forecast for early next week, the National Weather Service said.
Temperatures in the 30s and 40s are moving into the Northeast and are expected to last through Friday, the NWS said.
More moderate temperatures are forecast for the Northeast early next week, followed by another cold spell which will drag temperatures about 10 to 14 degrees below-normal.
In south Texas, the market ranged anywhere from $4.50 to the $4.70s, with most deals done in the low-$4.60s.
At the New York city-gate, prices jumped into the low-$5 area, up at least 40 cents from Wednesday.
Appalachian prices were up an average of 20 cents to the $4.50s.

Prospects of milder weather this weekend in the Midcontinent caused prices to soften sharply late in trading. On average, prices were down about five cents to the high-$4.60s, although early deals were reported done as high as $5.
Despite the slight warm-up in the Midwest this weekend, another cold front is expected to weigh on the thermometer early next week.

In west Texas, where most supplies are needed to the east and into the Texas and Midcontinent markets, Permian gas prices remained strong in the low-$4.80s. Deals were reported done anywhere from $4.70 to $4.95.
At the southern California border, prices gained more than five cents to about $4.60 as the Northwest awaited the arrival of much colder air and Rocky and Texas markets continued to draw on supplies.
